title: Applied ML Eval Integration & Standards: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates Redwood's standards and procedures for applied ML evaluation across the Eval Harness, Prompt Sets & Benchmarks, Model Onboarding, Quality Guardrails, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage teams. It is intended to be the single source of truth for evaluation engineering practices that ensure consistent fidelity, reproducibility, and operational readiness for models destined for serving in Redwood products (hosted, dedicated, private).

Goals and scope:
- Ensure every model passes a standardized onboarding pipeline with reproducible evals and documented failure modes.
- Provide a unified prompt-set catalog and benchmark definitions to measure quality regressions and feature-specific metrics.
- Define minimal quality guardrails (semantic, safety, performance) and quantization profiles for production variants.
- Formalize a regression triage workflow with SLAs, automated alerting, and rollout controls.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers, model owners, SREs, product owners, and platform engineers responsible for model serving and rollout.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Ownership: applied-ml-and-evals (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary), eng-sre (operational readiness).
- Roles:
  - Model Owner: responsible for providing model artifacts, training metadata, and initial evals.
  - Eval Engineer: runs the Eval Harness, ensures tests are reproducible, and curates prompt sets.
  - Release Engineer / SRE: validates performance (latency, memory), deploy config, and rollback policies.
  - Security/Compliance Reviewer: triages privacy/safety-sensitive outputs as needed.

Standards and artifacts (required for every model onboarding):
1) Eval Harness Integration:
   - CI job name: eval-harness/model-onboard/<model-name>/<version>.
   - Required outputs: per-prompt-set metrics JSON, token-level latency histogram, calibration curves (if applicable), and deterministic seed used for noisy metrics.
   - Example CLI: 
     - ./eval-harness run --model s3://models/<name>/<version> --config eval-configs/<name>.yaml --out reports/<name>-<version>.json

2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks:
   - Each model must be evaluated against:
     a) Core prompt suite (functional correctness across top-10 features).
     b) Safety suite (toxicity, PII leakage, hallucination probes).
     c) Customer-driven benchmarks (customer-specific critical prompt sets where applicable; redacted).
   - Prompt set metadata table (required columns): name | description | owner | intended-metric | schema-version | sample-count
     - Example: 
       Core-QA | closed-book QA across engineering docs | applied-ml | EM@1, EM@5, BLEU | v1.2 | 5000

3) Quality Guardrails (pass/fail and advisory):
   - Hard gates (must pass):
     * Safety threshold: Safety-check false-positive rate <= 1% for benchmarked toxicity probes.
     * Hallucination probe: factual-precision >= 85% on curated factual dataset.
     * Latency gate for production tier: p95 <= 300ms for hosted small models; p95 <= 1s for large models on Dedicated config.
   - Advisory checks (require engineering signoff if violated):
     * Style/fluency regressions > 5% relative drop versus baseline.
     * Cost-per-token estimates exceed target by >20% (flag for Optimize team).

4) Quantization Profiles and Validation:
   - Profiles: q4_0, q4_1, q8_0 (names and configuration stored in quantization-profiles repo).
   - For each profile, provide: absolute metric delta from baseline (FP16/FP32), per-prompt-set failure modes, and performance tradeoffs (tokens/sec, memory).
   - Validation matrix (required):
     - Model version | Profile | EM@1 delta | Safety delta | p95 latency | GPU memory (MiB)
     - Acceptance rule: EM@1 delta >= -2% AND Safety delta >= -0.5% AND p95 latency improves by >= 10% OR memory reduced by >= 20% to justify profile.

5) Regression Triage Playbook (incident-style for eval regressions):
   - Detection:
     1. Automated monitors (Eval Alerting) compare nightly onboarding-run results vs. baseline; alert thresholds configured in dashboards-and-alerts.
     2. On-call (applied-ml) receives alerts: severity levels defined below.
   - Severity thresholds:
     - Sev-1: Safety gate failure OR major functional regression (>15% relative loss on core metric). P1 page + immediate rollback.
     - Sev-2: Medium functional regression (5-15%) or latency breach impacting SLOs. 4-hour response, can require partial rollout pause.
     - Sev-3: Advisory/metric drift <5% — logged, owners notified for investigation within 7 days.
   - Triage steps (numbered):
     1. Acknowledge alert in incident tracker; tag model-owner and eval-engineer.
     2. Re-run Eval Harness locally with identical seed and hardware allocation; collect detailed logs (seed, RNG state, hardware topology).
     3. Compare per-prompt-set diffs and identify top-10 failing prompts.
     4. If reproducible: run ablation to isolate cause (prompt change, tokenizer diff, model weight delta, quantization profile).
     5. If not reproducible: escalate to eng-serving-runtime to validate runtime determinism and env parity.
     6. Publish triage summary to related_pages and tag for release decision (rollback, patch, or accept with mitigations).
   - Rollout controls: Canary at 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metric checks at each step. Automatic rollback triggers if metric delta exceeds configured thresholds at any step.

Operational SLOs and monitoring configuration:
- Eval harness CI: success rate >= 99% over 30 days. Failures cause automated retry and alert if persistent > 3 consecutive runs.
- Nightly regression scan: run every 24h against production baseline; alert on any hard gate failure.
- Dashboards (required): per-model metric trends, per-prompt-set heatmaps, token-latency percentiles, quantization-validation matrix.

Templates and examples (copy to use):
- eval-configs/model-example.yaml: includes seed, prompt-set list, metric buckets, and hardware profile.
- regressions/triage-template.md: quick checklist and findings table (root-cause, repro-steps, mitigation, owner, eta).
- quant-profiles/q4_1-example.json: example quantization parameters and expected memory footprint.

Example eval CLI snippet:
  ./eval-harness run --model s3://models/t5x-small/v2 --prompts core-qa,safety-suite --seed 42 --profile q4_1 --out reports/t5x-small-v2.json

Acceptance and release gating checklist (must be completed and referenced by release engineer):
1. Eval Harness report uploaded and passing all hard gates.
2. Quantization profile validated and delta metrics within acceptance rules.
3. Performance run (p95/p99) meets tier-specific SLOs and runbook steps validated.
4. Security and privacy review completed if prompts or outputs touch regulated domains.
5. Rollout plan with canary stages and automated rollback configured in deployment manifest.

FAQ / common failure modes and mitigations:
- "Non-deterministic eval failures": Common causes are RNG seeds, tokenization changes, or hardware topology differences. Mitigation: pin seeds, freeze tokenizer version, and run on standardized hardware profile.
- "Quantization causes hallucinations": Isolate via per-prompt-set diffs; if confined to low-frequency prompts, consider hybrid profile or mixed-precision fallback.
- "Nightly alert noise": Adjust thresholds for low-signal prompt sets and promote stable prompt-sets to baseline-only status.
